Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT A. Francisco Gold Condominium II Bldg, EDSA corner Mapagmahal St., Diliman, Quezon City LEGAL SERVICE OPINION NO. 79 S. 2010 03 June 2010 ATTY. CLETO L. EVANGELISTA JR. EVANGELISTA LAW OFFICE Rizal St., Ormoc City Dear Atty. Evangelista Jr.: This has reference to your letter dated 24 May 2010 seeking clarification on whether members Of the People's Law Enforcement Board (PLEB) are considered government officials or not, and if so, are they entitled to government travel expenses and official travels or seminars related to their work such as the Mandatory Continuing Legal Education (MCLE). In response thereto, it is this Department's view that membership to PLEB is not deemed a government service but a CIVIC DUTY as explicitly couched in the plain language of the law, particularly Section 69 of Republic Act No. 8551, otherwise known as the 'Philippine National Police Reform and Reorganization Act of 1998', amending Section 43 (c) of Republic Act No. 6975, otherwise known as the 'Department of the Interior and Local Government Act of 1 990', and we quote: "Section 69. Compensation and Benefits. — Paragraph c, Section 43 of Republic Act No. 6975 shall be amended to read as follocps: "(c) Compensation. — Membership in the PLEB is a civic duty. h-lmvever, PLEB members shall be paid per diem and shall be provided zoitIl life insurance coverage as may be determined by the city or nmnicipal cotmcil from city or municipal funds. The DILG shall provide for the per diem and insurance coverage of PLEB members in certain loto income municipalities. " Civic duty is a citizen's bounden duty or obligation as member or part of his community, as opposed to government or public service. The participation of private citizens in the PLEB is in consonance with one of the avowed objectives of the PLEB — that is, "to enhance civilian participation in the disciplinary process of errant PNP. The PLEB is part of the system of coordination and members and cooperation among the citizenry, local executives and PNP provided for in the law creating the Philippine National Police". 1 Fianza vs The PLEB, G.R. 109638-9, 31 march 1995

2 Premised on the foregoing, we resolve that PLEB membership being a civic duty, ergo, members thereof are not entitled to governmental travel expenses on official travels or seminars, and their compensation is limited only to the per diem that a city or municipal council may be determined from city or municipal funds. We hope that we have sufficiently addressed your concern. Very truly yours, By Authority of the Secretary: A Y. JES Director III B. DO Copy mrnished: Dir. Franciscn C.
